title: 2026-11-22 — CI's toolchain moves the build directory's layout

data.head: ## 2026-11-22 — CI's toolchain moves the build directory's layout

body: The CI runners took rustc 1.100.0 while the dev host stayed on cargo 1.99.0. On Cargo 1.100 a target package's build directory is `target/{triple}/debug/build/{package}/{hash}/` and a build script's printed output is `…/{hash}/run/stdout`; Cargo 1.99 keeps `build/{package}-{hash}/output`. The matrix witness of 2026-11-21-dependency-and-ci-debts, pinned to the 1.99 glob, read red on all four non-linux rows twice (CI#44965103559, CI#44967824760) before it read the build tree by content (CI#44971052397).

Any check that reads a build script's output — or any other path under `target/` — reads it by content or by a search that names no layout, and prints what it found, so the first CI run on a newer toolchain measures the layout instead of failing on a guess.

The session paid dependency and CI debts with no Rust source change: the yanked async-executor 1.14.0 moved to 1.14.1 in the lock, and no crate was added.
Every CI leg that builds skia (clippy, test, build, msrv, doc, coverage and a11y) now first fetches skia's prebuilt archive for its host, checks it against a committed sha256 record and points the build at the local copy; a refused archive ends the leg before any cargo run.
The fast leg's closing target sweep now runs under the same verified archive, and the per-platform test matrix gained a verify step and a witness step that reads red when a row's skia build did not read its verified archive.
The dependency audit's six advisory ignores stayed the same, each with a reworded reason naming the release it waits on, and the zip ignores are gone.
Measured: after the lock move, the stand's dependency graph still holds no accesskit platform adapter (the probe reads 0), and CI read green 17 of 17 checks on the final head.
A plan claim was disproved and dropped: forcing skia's binary download does not panic on a wrong key in a crates.io build, so a missing or wrong archive falls back to a full source build, which the witness then reads red.

body_fields.fact: The skia archive script takes TARGET DIR. Exit 0 prints one stdout line, the SKIA_BINARIES_URL template file://{DIR}/skia-binaries-{key}.tar.gz. Exit 1 prints skia-archive: attempt {n} of 3 failed in {fetch|verify}, then skia-archive: no verified archive. Exit 2 prints skia-archive: usage or skia-archive: no recorded archive for this target, with nothing fetched. A matching local copy is reused, and a fetched copy is renamed into place only when its sha256 equals the record.

The leg runner's SKIA_LEGS are clippy, test, build, msrv, doc, coverage and a11y. Each first verifies skia's archive for the rustc host into target/skia-archives and exports SKIA_BINARIES_URL, and a refused archive ends the leg before any cargo runs. The fast leg's closing target sweep runs under the same verified URL.
SKIA_BINARIES_URL is an occupied environment variable. The leg runner and the matrix test step set it, and skia-bindings' build script reads it. It holds a local file:// path template and no secret.

Skia's prebuilt archive is fetched once per platform from the rust-skia skia-binaries release at the locked skia-bindings tag and verified against a committed sha256 per target (five targets). FORCE_SKIA_BINARIES_DOWNLOAD is never set, because in a crates.io build it forces a full source build. A failed read or an unrecorded key falls back to a source build of skia, a stated limit.

The matrix test job verifies skia's archive after Setup and appends SKIA_BINARIES_URL to GITHUB_ENV. After the tests, a witness step reads every file under the target triple's skia-bindings build paths by content, with out/ pruned and only files under 1024 KiB. It passes only when a file holds both FROM: file:// and DOWNLOAD AND INSTALL SUCCEEDED, printing skia-archive: build output {path}:{line}. Otherwise it prints skia-archive: no skia-bindings build read the verified archive with the build tree and exits 1.

Any cargo run on the shared target directory without SKIA_BINARIES_URL re-runs skia-bindings' build script, because the script declares rerun-if-env-changed. Every cargo call in a skia-building leg, its sweep included, must therefore run under the verified URL.

Cargo 1.100 (the CI runners) puts a package's build-script output at build/skia-bindings/{hash}/run/stdout, while Cargo 1.99 (the dev host) keeps build/skia-bindings-{hash}/output. A check of build output must not pin one layout.

body: CI legs run through the leg script: the leg script gains a skia arm. For seven legs it fetches and verifies the recorded archive first and exports SKIA_BINARIES_URL, and a refused archive ends the leg with a non-zero exit before any cargo runs.
The CI leg script's exit-code contract: a leg can now also end non-zero because the archive script refused, before cargo. A row naming the leg script's exit codes may need that case.

Native platform CI matrix: the matrix test job gains two steps on every row. One is a verified-archive step that writes SKIA_BINARIES_URL into the job environment. The other is a witness step that exits 1 unless some skia-bindings build output names a file:// read and a successful install.

CI Python scripts unit-tested, and Python script tests under unittest: a new CI script with its own unittest file (13 cases) joins the ci-scripts leg through discovery. Rows that describe the leg as discovery over the CI scripts folder stay true.

Dependency audit (advisories and licenses): async-executor moved off its yanked release, the zip ignores are closed, and each of the six standing ignores now states the release it waits on or the residual row that owns it. The audit reads advisories ok and licenses ok with no yanked warning.
Cargo legs run locked: the lock moved by one entry, and the legs still run locked against it.

Build directory held by a sweep, and target sweep safe around a build: the fast leg's sweep now runs under the verified SKIA_BINARIES_URL. A cargo run on the shared target without that variable re-runs skia-bindings' build script.
Workspace tested in the fast CI leg: the fast leg's closing sweep now fetches the verified archive first, and its failure is still swallowed by the sweep's own or-true.
Minimum supported Rust version and MSRV verified by build: the msrv leg is a skia-building leg, so it now builds skia from the verified archive.
Coverage leg gated by the floors, a11y leg membership and clippy legs: each of these legs now runs the verified-archive arm before cargo. No floor, membership or clippy scope moved.

Host-reproducible CI legs, local pre-push gate and local baseline: on the dev host the leg runner now fetches the archive over the network into a folder under target and reuses a matching local copy, so a local leg needs the archive or its release.

Bounded, retried package installs: the archive fetch is a new bounded network fetch in CI (120 s timeout, 3 attempts 10 s apart). A rule that bounds and retries installs may now cover it, or need to say that it does not.
CI uses no secrets, read-only permissions, and actions pinned to commit SHAs: the new matrix steps add no action, permission or secret. SKIA_BINARIES_URL holds a local path template, not a secret.

Leg log and CI log artifacts, and leg logs uploaded on failure: the archive script's fixed stderr lines now land in the leg log or the step log. On failure, the witness prints the build outputs it found and the skia-bindings build tree to the step log.

Shared workspace test cache and shared CI build cache: verified archives are kept under the shared target, and a cargo run without the URL on that target invalidates skia-bindings' build script result.

Tests controlled red-before-green: the controls on the archive sum check and the URL export held, and a learning recorded on 2026-11-14 did not recur: a gate control on a ci-scripts unittest case no longer reads INDETERMINATE.

body_fields.fact: The leg script's skia-building legs (clippy, test, build, msrv, doc, coverage and a11y) each fetch and verify the recorded skia archive and run every cargo call, including the fast leg's target sweep, under SKIA_BINARIES_URL. A refused archive ends the leg before cargo, and legs that build no skia set no skia variable.

Every row of the native platform matrix fetches and verifies its target's recorded skia archive after setup. After test, a witness step reads red unless a skia-bindings build output names a file:// read and DOWNLOAD AND INSTALL SUCCEEDED.

Skia's prebuilt fallback is a stated limit. A failed archive read or a build asking for an unrecorded key falls back to a full source build of skia with no panic. The matrix witness reads it red on CI, and the dev host's file:// output check reads it red locally. FORCE_SKIA_BINARIES_DOWNLOAD is never set, because in a crates.io build it forces a source build.

The skia archive witness reads skia-bindings' build tree by content and not by a pinned path. A CI toolchain ahead of the dev host moves the layout: Cargo 1.100 writes build-script output to run/stdout under a hashed folder, while Cargo 1.99 writes the output file.

The skia archive script's exit codes: 0 prints one SKIA_BINARIES_URL template line; 1 means no verified archive after 3 attempts, with a fixed stderr line for each attempt; 2 means a bad call or an unrecorded target, with nothing fetched.
A hosted-runner cancel with no runner is a hosted-runner limit, answered by a hand re-run. The cancelled-runner watch is retired by its rule after a 60-run census.
